search_log: Searched official author and publisher excerpts for "The Great Alone" by Kristin Hannah and opened sustained versions on Kristin Hannah's site and St. Martin's Press.
Searched "The Great Alone" with point of view, third person, narrator, and alternating-narration terms; opened BookRags and LitCharts whole-book POV descriptions.

Searched exact first-person quotation "Books are the mile markers of my life" and verified through the LitCharts Chapter 17 analysis and an interior chapter rendering that it is Leni's personal statement.
Searched exact passages beginning "I was taught by my father" and verified they continue the headed PERSONAL STATEMENT by Lenora Allbright.
Searched the exact "Wild. That's how I describe it all" passage and late-novel chapter analyses; results attribute it to an embedded Lily Walker text rather than the base narrator.
Searched Chapters 30-31 and the ending structure; SuperSummary and LitCharts identify the concluding first-person material as an article written by Leni.

Checked an interior Chapter 31 rendering after one LitCharts summary used loose 'first-person perspective' wording for Matthew's focalization; the actual scene remains third-person narration with occasional direct thoughts, so it does not establish alternating base narration.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, predominantly limited through Leni, with occasional third-person focal shifts to other characters. Numerous Goodreads passages independently show sustained external narration naming Leni and reporting her perceptions, while authorized author and publisher excerpts show the same construction. The apparent first-person counterevidence is local material: q02472 and q02542 are portions of Leni's headed college personal statement, and q02528 is an embedded text attributed to Lily Walker. Dialogue, aphorisms, generic you, and direct thoughts likewise do not change the base person. Whole-book POV descriptions corroborate THIRD, and no credible source establishes sustained first- or second-person base sections; the only limitation is that the Tier A excerpts cover the opening rather than every chapter.
